title: Stolen session token used against room WebSocket
scenario: A valid player session token is observed from a new network and used to open a room WebSocket while the real player is active. No recovery-key or database compromise is assumed.
severityReason: A stolen credential can expose personalized room state and may alter an authoritative match; hidden-information or winner integrity impact is SEV-1.

timeline.evidence: Synthetic alert: concurrent use of one session fingerprint from two networks.
SEV-1 declared, restricted record opened, five response roles assigned.
Affected account sessions revoked, socket closed, matchmaking paused for the synthetic cohort, room revision preserved.
Synthetic patch passed credential, origin, revocation and full-game regression gates and met the canary decision checklist.
No production exposure occurred; tabletop gaps and follow-ups were assigned.

followUps.action: Run a human staging drill that proves pager delivery and role handoff.
Exercise the private player-notification and status-page approval path.

limitations: No production credential, player data, pager or public status channel was used.
Human paging, role handoff and external communication remain quarterly staging exercises.
